card.summary: Free plan: unlimited projects and unlimited publishes; each project capped at 450 MB and 10,100 files. No account-level byte quota.

free_tier.stated: Free plan: unlimited projects and unlimited publishes; each project capped at 450 MB and 10,100 files. No account-level byte quota.

per_object_cap.stated: no per-file cap documented but it inherits the project cap

egress.terms: No bandwidth quota or metering is documented anywhere on the free plan; every project is served from all 10 of Surge's own edge nodes ('Every project. Free or paid. Serves from all of them').

record.tooling: Official `surge` CLI (npm, ~free) and a documented raw REST deploy API: PUT /:domain with Basic auth, Content-Type: application/gzip, a gzipped tarball body plus file-count and project-size headers. That is directly scriptable, no CLI needed.
record.chaining: Allows unlimited projects per account with each project capped at 450 MB. Free accounts register via command-line without payment credentials. Sharding divides data across independent project directories.

limits.value: no per-file cap documented but it inherits the project cap

record.limits_note: 450 MB and 10,100 files per project (hard: 'Aborted - Unable to publish. Application too large'); no bandwidth figure published; no per-file cap documented but it inherits the project cap. Re-publishing replaces the whole project (full-sync deploy), so appending one file re-uploads the directory.
record.reliability_note: Deploy is full-replace, not incremental. A slow link makes each publish expensive. Free tier has no stated SLA and no published bandwidth ceiling, so behaviour at 1 TiB/day is unproven.

evidence.proved: 'Projects are limited to 10,100 files and 450 MB.'
'The core of Surge costs nothing, without trial windows or project caps: Unlimited projects and publishes'
'PUT /:domain ... The body is a gzipped tar archive ... file-count / project-size headers'
